title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 2

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When does the CV workshop begin?
tasks.audioText: The careers office is offering a CV workshop on Friday afternoon. It begins at one thirty in Room 24. Bring a draft CV saved on a USB drive or in your college cloud folder. The adviser will show students how to describe practical skills and organise education details. There will also be time to ask individual questions. Places are limited, so book online before Thursday.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which document should students bring to the CV workshop?

The adviser will show students how to describe practical skills and organise education details. There will also be time to ask individual questions. tasks.prompt: Nikita is applying for a summer placement in an electronics workshop. In his CV, he describes a college project in which he assembled a training circuit and recorded test results. He lists teamwork, careful measurement and basic computer skills. His tutor suggests replacing the phrase 'I am good at everything' with specific examples that an employer can understand. Reading 1. What project does Nikita describe?
What does the tutor recommend changing?
options: A general claim into specific examples

tasks.prompt: Choose the correct comparative: 'This version of my CV is ___ than the first one.'
Choose TWO strong ways to describe a skill in a CV.
options: Use a vague claim without evidence

tasks.prompt: Complete: 'A short period of practical work in a company is a work ___.'
A careers adviser asks you to explain a skill. What should you do?
options: Say that you have every skill.
Give a brief example of when you used it.

tasks.prompt: Put the following steps for tailoring a CV to a specific role in a logical order.
Write 60–80 words describing three skills you could include in a CV. Give a short example of how you developed or used each skill.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: three distinct skills are identified (0–2); each skill is supported by a relevant example of how it was developed or used (0–2); examples are clearly expressed with understandable grammar (0–2); CV/employability vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
